q: What is the capital of Canada?
note: Queen Victoria settled on Ottawa in 1857 as a compromise between rival cities including Toronto and Quebec City.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
note: Canberra was built from scratch as a compromise capital because Sydney and Melbourne could not agree.

q: Which is the largest country in the world by land area?
note: Russia is so wide that it shares a land border with Norway in the northwest and North Korea in the far east.

q: Cairo is the capital of which country?
note: Cairo sits at the head of the Nile Delta, where the river fans out toward the Mediterranean.

q: Stockholm is the capital of which Scandinavian country?
note: Stockholm is spread across more than a dozen islands where a large lake drains into the Baltic Sea.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
note: The city was called Edo until 1868, when the emperor moved there and it was renamed Tokyo, or "eastern capital."

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
note: Brasilia was purpose-built in the empty interior and took over as capital from Rio de Janeiro in 1960.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
note: Ankara replaced Istanbul as the capital in 1923, when the Turkish republic was founded.

q: Which tiny country sits high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain?
note: Andorra has been governed since 1278 by two co-princes: the French head of state and a Spanish bishop.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
note: Wellington is the southernmost capital city of any sovereign country.

q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
note: Lesotho is one of only three countries in the world entirely enclosed by a single other country.

q: What is the capital of Morocco?
note: Casablanca and Marrakesh are better known abroad, but the government sits in Rabat on the Atlantic coast.

q: Which South American country takes its name from the Spanish word for the equator?
note: The equator itself passes just north of the capital, Quito.

q: Which South American country has two capitals, La Paz and Sucre?
note: Sucre is the constitutional capital, while the government does its business up in La Paz.

q: Which is the smallest sovereign country in the world by area?
note: The whole country covers about 110 acres, tucked inside the city of Rome.

q: What is the capital of Switzerland?
note: Zurich and Geneva are larger and more famous, but Bern has held the federal government since 1848.

q: Which African country was settled by freed American slaves and declared independence in 1847?
note: Its capital, Monrovia, is named after US President James Monroe.

q: Ljubljana is the capital of which European country?
note: Slovenia broke away from Yugoslavia in 1991 after a conflict that lasted only ten days.

q: Which is the only country with coastline on both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
note: Iran was known internationally as Persia until it asked the world to use its own name in 1935.

q: Which country governs the western half of the island of New Guinea?
note: The eastern half is the separate country of Papua New Guinea, and the border is a nearly straight line.
